title: Entanglement Asymmetry and Asymmetry Contour under Boundary Symmetry Breaking
abstract: We investigate how symmetry-breaking boundary magnetic fields affect magnetization and Rényi-2 entanglement asymmetry (EA) in the transverse-field Ising model. For the ground state, magnetization exhibits qualitatively distinct behaviors in the ordered and disordered phases. EA also exhibits phase-dependent behavior, which is well captured by the lower and upper bounds derived in this work. In the critical regime, both magnetization and EA exhibit behavior qualitatively consistent with the field-theoretical predictions for a related setup. We also study boundary-quench dynamics and find that magnetization propagates from the boundary into the bulk with a velocity consistent with the maximum quasiparticle velocity. In contrast, because EA is a subsystem-integrated quantity, its spatial structure is not directly resolved. We therefore introduce the asymmetry contour, a contour-like finite-difference quantity that provides a spatially resolved characterization of the symmetry-breaking information encoded in the reduced density matrix. The resulting contour is complementary to the local magnetization, retaining sensitivity to nonlocal many-body correlations while its dynamics also reflects the underlying quasiparticle propagation. These results show how EA and its contour can provide complementary information-theoretic characterizations of symmetry breaking and its spatial structure.
summary: This work analyzes how boundary magnetic fields break symmetry in the transverse-field Ising model, examining both magnetization and entanglement asymmetry (EA). The authors introduce the Asymmetry Contour (AC) as a novel, spatially resolved diagnostic tool that successfully captures the non-local information encoded in the reduced density matrix, providing a powerful complement to local measurements.
main_problem: The paper investigates how symmetry-breaking boundary magnetic fields affect magnetization and Rényi-2 entanglement asymmetry (EA) in the transverse-field Ising model, and develops a spatially resolved measure for this information.
main_result: The newly introduced Asymmetry Contour (AC) provides a spatially resolved characterization of symmetry-breaking information, complementing local magnetization by retaining sensitivity to non-local many-body correlations.
method: The analysis employs fermionic representations (Jordan-Wigner transformation) to map the problem onto a quadratic fermionic Hamiltonian, allowing the calculation of entanglement measures and dynamics.
model_or_system: The system studied is the transverse-field Ising model (TFIM) on a 1D lattice with open boundary conditions, perturbed by symmetry-breaking boundary magnetic fields.
key_observables: Magnetization ($\langle X_i angle$), Rényi-2 Entanglement Asymmetry (EA), and the novel Asymmetry Contour (AC).
important_parameters: The ratio of coupling constants ($J/h$), boundary field strength ($h_b$), and the system size ($L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on perturbative expansions (for small $h_b$ or $J/h$ ratios) and the use of fermionic approximations derived from the Hamiltonian diagonalization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase-dependent behavior of magnetization and EA, and show color maps comparing the calculated Asymmetry Contour (AC) against Exact Diagonalization (ED) results over space and time.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the system and observables, calculating the ground state properties (magnetization, EA) in various phases, and finally introducing and analyzing the Asymmetry Contour (AC) to provide a full spatial characterization of the symmetry breaking dynamics.
why_interesting: The development of the Asymmetry Contour is a significant theoretical advance, offering a tool to map non-local, information-theoretic properties (like entanglement asymmetry) onto a spatially resolved picture, which is crucial for understanding boundary effects in quantum dynamics.
